- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, showing a persistent lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 65→68) and fails to correct quickly, leading to overcorrection in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds high values too long after peaks, failing to reflect natural price pullback.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually drift lower, but not in sync with true volatility patterns.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when recent history includes strong upward trends, and underestimates when trends are weak or downward.
